name: Flash

today.normal: 5–8 golds, 1–3 traps before each (half gold look-alikes), traps 0.6 s long, gold up 1.5 s, 60 s
today.hard: 6–8 golds, 2–3 traps, 75 % look-alikes, gold up 1.5 s
today.expert: 8 golds, 3–5 traps, 75 % look-alikes, gold up 1 s

measured: Elite held to human limits 124 / 114 / 106 / 100 (Expert best tenth 123); 140 ms elite 188 / 186 / 187 / 183 (speed-levels-tune, 100 deals). Average player: not documented.
easy: 5 golds; the first inside 3 s with no trap before it (today 4–7 s); 0–1 plain trap before the others and no look-alikes (as today); gold up 1.5 s.
hard: 8 golds; 2–3 traps before each (about 20 a round against Normal's 13), each 0.45 s long and 0.6–1 s apart, the first inside the first second; 75 % gold look-alikes; gold up 0.9 s.
expert: 9 golds; 6–8 traps before each (about 63 a round), each 0.35 s long and 0.5–0.65 s apart (never more than two a second); 90 % look-alikes; gold up 0.6 s.

glance.easy: A calm dark glass; the first gold arrives within three seconds.
glance.hard: Trap colours fire about once a second from the start.
glance.expert: The glass flickers twice a second, nearly all gold look-alikes.

why: The only thing Flash can ask beyond a fast finger is not to be fooled, so the traps multiply and quicken while the gold's own window never drops below 0.6 s, more than twice the 0.25 s limit.
proof: Open by design (a reaction game). At 0.25 s a gold pays 115 on tapRev 7's curve, so with the 15-point steady hand the limits player tops out at 130 on every level, Normal included (measured through the server's grader: 250 ms 130, 200 ms 135, 170 ms 165, 140 ms 190 at all four levels). Expert's 200 needs I1's tapRev 8 with the curve's full mark at 250 ms (I1 as written, 250 ms = 150, still caps the limits player at 165). With that, playFlashHuman in scripts/speed-levels-tune.ts must reach 200 in its best tenth at Expert, pinned in scripts/speed-levels-check.ts.
stamp: Level field only: the deal stamps flashMs (as today) and a new trapMs that the stage and replayFlash read. Expert's 200 also needs I1's tapRev 8 (Joe's scoring decision).
risk: The scoring curve, not the level, caps a 0.25 s player at 130 on every level (115 a gold plus the 15-point steady hand). Level design can only change how often a player is fooled; it cannot lift that cap, so no Expert reaches 200 under the limits until a scoring change (I1's tapRev 8, which as written still stops at 165). The average kit is already at its floor (17) on any Expert of 36 traps or more, and fast full-screen flashes must stay under three a second.

evidence.easy: measured: today's Easy (the first gold inside 3 s needs builder code), speed-levels-tune players, 100 deals: average kit 91, limits 122 (best tenth 131), 140 ms elite 188. A run on exactly 250 ms scores 130.
evidence.hard: measured: adjusted Hard built by hand in memory (8 golds, 2–3 traps, 75 % look-alikes, gold 0.9 s), 100 deals: average kit 35, limits 106 (best 131). As first proposed (3–5 traps) it scored 21 and 99, the same as today's Expert (24 and 100).
evidence.expert: measured: built by hand in memory (9 golds, 6–8 traps, 90 % look-alikes, gold 0.6 s), 100 deals: average kit 17 (its floor), limits 69 (best 107), 140 ms elite 180. Exactly 250 ms scores 130, so no run reached 200.

verdict: adjusted: Hard's traps cut from 3–5 to 2–3 before each gold (about 20 a round) because 3–5 scored the same as today's Expert; the average kit now steps 91, 71, 35, 17, and Expert's 200 stays out of reach under the limits on today's curve (130 at most).
limitsToday: scripts/speed-levels-tune.ts:134 playFlashHuman (250 ± 25 ms reactions plus lure taps) under the tool's own HUMAN_LIMITS (:32); scripts/speed-levels-check.ts:215-220 asserts on 100 deals that Easy is no harder than Normal, Hard and Expert are each 3 lower, and Expert's best tenth is at least min(140, Normal's average), which for Flash is Normal's 114. Nothing asserts 200. level-tune.ts --human-limits plays the plain kits and ignores the flag for puzzles (level-tune.ts:163).
